I like this idea but it is vulnerable to a number of biases.

  1. It assumes everyone in your target group uses voat.

  2. It assumes everyone in your target group has access to a computer.

  3. It assumes your target group has access to the internet.

  4. Only people that have an interest in the survey will respond.

All of these factors will have a strong influence on the group of people you are trying to survey. This influence may stop your survey from being applicable to a larger population. I would use this sub as a way to supplement other surveying methods.

When you experience something strange in Chrome that your other browsers don't also do:

  1. Open your extensions page (chrome://extensions or use the "three lines" menu button).
  2. Look for anything strange or new.
  3. Check that each enabled extension does NOT have the "Allow in incognito" box checkmarked.
  4. Open an incognito window (from the menu or keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+N).
  5. Go through the steps you took to find the error before this.

Usually in a situation like this, one of two things is happening: 1) a spyware extension has been installed and is hijacking your browsing, or 2) the website you're using displays radically different pages based on your user-agent info. It's almost always the first one.
